detailed_rationale:
Tejas Networks is a Tata-group-controlled (via Panatone Finvest) telecom equipment maker (optical, wireless, FTTx, 5G radio products). Q1 FY27 showed a sequential improvement -- revenue of Rs 402 crore, up 21% from Rs 333 crore in Q4 FY26, driven by international 5G radio shipments and domestic 100G/400G optical and FTTx demand, with the net loss narrowing slightly to Rs 202 crore from Rs 211 crore. The company also registered its first commercial win for an end-to-end 5G network deployment in South America. The quant CSV's revenue_growth_1y figure of roughly -87.6% (measured on a trailing/TTM basis as of the Mar 2026 cut) reflects a large year-ago comparison base -- most likely a lumpy large government/defence order recognized in the prior period that did not repeat -- rather than a live deterioration; per standard practice, the fresher sequential quarterly trend is used as the operative read here rather than escalating the stale TTM comparison.

Even using the more favorable sequential read, the fundamentals remain weak: the company is still posting a substantial quarterly loss (Rs 202 crore), net debt is very heavy relative to its size (gross debt of roughly Rs 4,866 crore against cash of only Rs 589 crore, i.e., net debt of roughly Rs 4,277 crore versus a market cap of just Rs 9,729 crore), and the order book of Rs 1,529 crore provides only thin, roughly one-year-of-revenue visibility for an equipment maker. ROE of -4.65%, ROCE of 3.4%, D/E of 1.43, and negative interest coverage (-2.25x) all confirm the business is not generating adequate returns or covering its financing costs from operations.

A sequential revenue uptick and a first international 5G win are genuine positives worth noting, but they do not come close to offsetting a business still burning substantial cash, carrying very heavy net debt relative to its market value, and holding only a thin forward order book -- there is no basis to override the quant Sell.
recommendation_rationale: Despite a sequential revenue improvement, the company remains deeply loss-making (Rs 202 crore quarterly loss), carries net debt of roughly Rs 4,277 crore against a market cap of under Rs 10,000 crore, and has only a thin ~Rs 1,529 crore order book for an equipment maker. That combination of heavy leverage, continued cash burn, and limited backlog visibility leaves no basis for a rescue to Hold.
summary: Tejas Networks' quarterly revenue improved sequentially on the back of 5G radio and optical product shipments, including a first commercial win in South America, but the company remains deeply loss-making and carries a very heavy debt load relative to its size. We would not hold through this level of ongoing cash burn and leverage.
positive_para: Revenue grew 21% sequentially to Rs 402 crore on international 5G radio shipments and domestic optical/FTTx demand, the net loss narrowed slightly quarter-on-quarter, and the company secured its first end-to-end 5G network deployment win in South America -- a genuine, if early, sign of international traction for its wireless portfolio.
negative_para: The company is still losing roughly Rs 202 crore per quarter, and net debt of approximately Rs 4,277 crore against a market capitalization of under Rs 10,000 crore is a very heavy leverage burden for a business not yet generating positive operating returns (ROCE 3.4%, ROE -4.65%, interest coverage -2.25x). The order book of Rs 1,529 crore provides only thin, roughly one-year visibility for an equipment manufacturer, leaving limited assurance that the recent sequential improvement is durable.
reverse_dcf_judgment: With ROE and interest coverage both negative and net debt several times the size of annual revenue, there is no current earnings base to run a reverse-DCF against; the business needs a sustained multi-quarter run of revenue growth and margin improvement just to approach breakeven, let alone justify carrying the current debt load, and the thin order book does not yet provide that assurance.
